summary.intent: Land the callisto 0.12.0 release (consolidate changesets, merge the PR stack, merge the release PR), triage a stale issue, then start working through safe follow-up items grouped into stacked PRs that avoid the future michi-graph and pipeline work.
summary.outcome: Stack #300/#302/#303 merged, release PR #248 regenerated with 26 changes and merged, 0.12.0 verified on crates.io and GitHub, and stale issue #37 closed. Follow-up work began: PR A (floating v1 major tag) was implemented with tests and docs and opened, while the remaining items are not yet started.

repo: Changesets are consolidated by merging related entries; callisto status --check --strict validates the result (exit 0, all five crates pending a minor bump). It also prints three warnings about odd leftover tag candidates like callisto-graph@0.
Native GitHub stacks auto-retarget a stacked PR to main when the base PR merges, so no manual retarget is needed. Merge from the bottom up.

The release PR (callisto/version-packages) is pushed by the workflow token, so GitHub starts no CI on its head. Checks must be triggered manually (close/reopen or a push from a person or App token) before merging if protection requires them.
The release PR body template says 'All changes are backward compatible', which is wrong for 0.12.0. The changelog entries are accurate.

The Release workflow's execute job only runs after the release PR merges. It publishes crates to crates.io, creates tags, and creates the GitHub release with three binaries (aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-linux-gnu, x86_64-linux-musl).
callisto-fixtures is a dev-only crate and is intentionally not published to crates.io.

ADR 5 ('system Git only') removed the gix backend and callisto-vcs (106 fewer crates). callisto_model::vcs now has a single GitAccess type that shells out to git, which eliminated the yanked bisync 0.3.0 dependency chain.

Areas that would conflict with michi-graph/pipeline work: callisto-graph/src/toposort.rs, link_publish_prerequisites and the operation index in derive.rs, release-plan validation in callisto-model/src/release/intent.rs, release_execution.rs, the #290 guard, and the layered publish.
The E320 check follows the commit that set a package's own literal version, so workspace-inherited versions aren't covered. #290 merged with that gap and Codex found others.

The floating v1 tag work touched .github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh, callisto-release.yml, the setup-callisto install-callisto.sh named-ref resolution, its ref-resolution test, the justfile, and docs/releasing.md. Workflow policy tests constrain which steps may appear in the execute job.

code.finding: Named-ref resolution was extended so `uses: ...@v1` installs the matching release; covered by tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh.
New script that moves the floating major tag, with a test in .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh; wired into the execute job of callisto-release.yml.

workflow: Verify stack/merge state with a state script and a wait-for-run script instead of assuming; re-read PR checks and bodies before telling the user it is ready.
Outward-facing actions (closing issues, merging) were left for explicit user approval; the issue was closed only after the user said so.
Check claims against the repo (Cargo.lock, deny.toml, ADRs) before declaring an issue stale.
Run workflow contract tests and zizmor locally before opening workflow-touching PRs.
The assistant misstated that the stacked PR 'will need a retarget'; the user's question corrected it. Verify stack mechanics before stating them.

open_items: PR A (floating v1 tag) was opened; the remaining planned PRs are not yet started: publish deadline (configurable limit plus no-output limit) and the pnpm hang investigation, and the registry-metadata vs origin warning.
Layered publish with joint verify needs the user's sign-off, since it relaxes ADR 3 for npm/PyPI dependents.
Rework the #290 guard by dropping the history lookup and checking where the executor adopts an already-published version.
